checks.open_questions_explicit: FAIL - see finding below; a real open question is NOT listed in §11 and is instead silently resolved by assertion in §5.1

result.critical_finding: Design §5.1 asserts, as settled fact, that get_instance_state's script-supplied instance_id argument may name ANY instance the calling tenant owns ('any instance the calling tenant owns is a legitimate target... e.g. a parent instance reading a known child's state'), not merely the instance the script is itself running on behalf of. This is a same-tenant, cross-instance AUTHORIZATION decision, distinct from the tenant-boundary (prefix) question the design otherwise handles rigorously. It is NOT grounded in any cited source: not in REQ-159's requirement text or its 8 acceptance criteria (docs/requirements.yaml, checked directly -- AC3 only requires 'valid instance' vs 'invalid instance', silent on cross-instance scope), not in LUA-11/LUA-13's text, not in decision 0014 (which only speaks to cross-tenant prefix isolation, (e)), and not in R-Co's host_api/mod.zig capability comment reproduced in REQ-157's design (which only names the instance:read capability string, not a scoping rule). The 'parent instance reading a known child's state' scenario is invented in-place to justify the unrestricted read; no parent/child instance relationship concept has been established anywhere in the artifacts read for this design. This means: any script holding instance:read (a capability grant, not an identity check) can read ANY other instance's full state and variables within the same tenant, and the design treats this as intentionally in-scope rather than flagging it as a decision requiring REVIEWER/product sign-off. Per this workflow's own discipline (open questions must be explicit, not silently resolved), this is exactly the failure mode: a security-relevant scope decision was made silently, inside justificatory prose, instead of being surfaced in §11's Open Questions alongside OQ-1/OQ-2.
result.required_fix: Either (a) restrict get_instance_state to the execution_context.instance_id itself by default -- i.e. require the script-supplied instance_id to equal execution_context.instance_id, returning a structured error (e.g. reason: "forbidden") otherwise -- unless a cited source (requirement text, decision record, or explicit REVIEWER-approved addendum) establishes that cross-instance reads within a tenant are intended; or (b) if unrestricted same-tenant cross-instance reads really are intended, move this to an explicit Open Question in §11 (not resolved by design-author assertion) naming exactly what is unresolved -- whether Letflow's process model has any parent/child or ownership relationship between instances, and who (REVIEWER or a future requirement) decides the authorization scope -- rather than asserting a policy invented for this design alone. Remove or replace the unsupported 'parent instance reading a known child's state' justification in §5.1 with a citation or an OQ entry.
